prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (ideology removed)

- Economy and tax: Continue deficit reduction toward a balanced budget by the mid-2020s. Keep VAT rate unchanged; raise personal allowance to £12,500 and higher-rate threshold to £50,000 by 2020. Cut corporation tax to 17%. Reform and simplify business rates and tax system.

- Trade and regulation: Negotiate a new UK‑EU trade partnership; replicate existing EU trade deals; lodge UK WTO schedules; introduce a Trade Bill; create overseas Trade Commissioners and reconvene a Board of Trade. Reduce regulatory burdens; review utility and transport regulation.

- Corporate rules: Strengthen action on tax evasion; bolster pension scheme protections; tighten takeover scrutiny and make bid undertakings enforceable; publish executive pay ratios and give shareholders annual binding votes; require stronger employee voice on boards.

- Industrial strategy: Increase R&D to 2.4% of GDP within 10 years; expand university investment funds; deploy a £23bn productivity fund; create “Future Britain” sovereign-style funds; support key sectors (manufacturing, life sciences, digital, creative) and SMEs; improve late payment.

- Energy: Commission a cost-of-energy review; launch an industrial energy efficiency scheme; back offshore wind and island wind; develop shale gas with a new regulator, streamlined planning, and a Shale Wealth Fund.

- Infrastructure: Invest in HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail, Heathrow expansion, roads, rail capacity, cycling; promote EVs (aim for nearly all cars/vans to be zero-emission by 2050).

- Places: Move civil service and cultural bodies out of London; support city deals and local industrial strategies; expand cultural funding; improve urban design, trees, litter and road conditions.

- Rural and coastal: Maintain total farm support this parliament; design a new UK agri‑environment system; mandate CCTV in slaughterhouses; consider controls on live exports; protect post offices and rural services; extend the Coastal Communities Fund; create a new UK fisheries regime and withdraw from the London Fisheries Convention.

- Union and funding: Respect and extend devolution where appropriate; create a UK Shared Prosperity Fund to reduce regional inequalities.

- Brexit and law: Leave the single market and customs union; pass a Great Repeal Bill converting EU law; create common UK frameworks with devolved administrations; exclude the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights; retain ECHR membership this parliament; final deal subject to parliamentary votes.

- Defence and security: Meet NATO 2% with real-terms increases; retain nuclear deterrent; invest £178bn in equipment; support veterans; form a national infrastructure police force; fold the SFO into the NCA; strengthen cyber security.

- Justice and democracy: Introduce voter ID; complete boundary review to 600 MPs; retain first-past-the-post for national and extend to PCC/mayors; repeal the Fixed-term Parliaments Act; reform prisons and community sentencing; enhance victims’ rights.

- Immigration and asylum: Reduce net migration to sustainable levels; tighten non‑EU routes and student rules; control EU migration post‑Brexit; launch an integration strategy; establish a Commission for Countering Extremism. Prioritise resettlement from regions of conflict and support councils and community sponsors.

- Education and skills: Expand free schools; allow new selective schools with conditions; require universities/independent schools to sponsor state schools; open more maths schools; adjust faith school admissions rules. Introduce T‑levels, longer teaching hours, mandatory work placements; create institutes of technology; expand apprenticeships; discount travel for apprentices; provide a UCAS‑style technical portal. Increase school funding by £4bn by 2022; protect Pupil Premium; replace universal infant lunches with free breakfasts.

- Work and welfare: Raise the National Living Wage as a share of median pay; act on gig‑economy protections; continue Universal Credit rollout; offer NIC holidays for employers hiring specified disadvantaged groups.

- Health and social care: Increase NHS funding by at least £8bn real terms; expand training places; invest in buildings and tech; verify eligibility and raise the Immigration Health Surcharge; faster access to new treatments; expand seven‑day services; retain A&E and elective targets; recruit up to 10,000 more mental health staff. Social care: include home value in means test for home/residential care with a £100,000 asset floor and universal deferred payments; consult on system improvements; means‑test Winter Fuel Payments; retain other pensioner benefits; replace the pension “triple lock” with a “double lock” from 2020.

- Housing: Deliver 1.5m homes by 2022; protect Green Belt; higher‑quality, higher‑density design; council housing deals for new fixed‑term social homes with a later Right to Buy; reform compulsory purchase; capture land value for infrastructure.

- Families and equality: Expand 30 hours’ childcare and create more nursery places; act on gender and ethnicity pay gaps; modernise mental health law; target disability employment and access improvements; introduce a Domestic Violence and Abuse Bill; halve rough sleeping by 2022 and end it by 2027.

- Digital: Establish a Digital Charter; new data protection law, a Data Use and Ethics Commission, and a right to delete data at 18; continue major cyber investment. Expand full‑fibre, 5G, and mobile coverage; ensure Wi‑Fi on mainline trains; roll out Verify and open data; create a unified geospatial data body. Media: no second Leveson Inquiry; repeal Section 40.

- Consumer costs: Strengthen regulators and redress; cap poor‑value energy tariffs and roll out smart meters; improve rail ticketing and set minimum service levels during strikes; tackle rogue practices (cold calls, whiplash, parking); introduce a debt “Breathing Space.”
